title: The YM2610 OPNB registers
covers: the registers of the YM2610 (OPNB) as Yamaha's application manual draws them, and what MAME does for each

rows.text: The SSG registers are listed in a table headed Read/Write Data(SSG).
The table columns are ADDR., D7 to D0 and COMMENT.
$00 is Fine Tune and $01 is Coarse Tune, together the Channel-A Tone Period.
$02 is Fine Tune and $03 is Coarse Tune, together the Channel-B Tone Period.
$04 is Fine Tune and $05 is Coarse Tune, together the Channel-C Tone Period.
The Fine Tune cell is drawn across D7 to D0; the Coarse Tune cell of $01, $03 and $05 is drawn with a filled left half.
$06 is the Noise Period; its cell reads Period Control.
The left part of the $06 cell is drawn filled.
$07 is /Enable; its cell is split into /Noise and /Tone parts after a filled left part.
The left part of the $07 cell is drawn filled.
MAME's SSG register accessors take bits 7 and 6 of $07 as the I/O port B and A directions, and bits 5-3 and 2-0 as the noise and tone enables.
$08, $09 and $0A are the Channel-A, Channel-B and Channel-C Amplitude.
Each amplitude cell is drawn as a filled left part, then M, then Level.
MAME takes bit 4 of $08 to $0A as the envelope enable of the channel and bits 3-0 as its amplitude.
$0B is the Fine Tune of the Envelop Period (spelled so in the capture).
The $0B cell is one Fine Tune cell over the full width of the table.
$0C is the Coarse tune of the Envelop Period (spelled so in the capture).
The $0C cell is one Coarse tune cell over the full width of the table.
$21 is Test, commented LSI Test Data.
The $21 cell is drawn across the full width of the table.
$22 is LFO Freq Control; its cell is a filled left half and an LFO cell.
The left half of the $22 cell is drawn filled.
In the description of $22, D3 is LFO ON and D2 to D0 are FREQ CONT; D7 to D4 are drawn filled.
FREQ CONT is set from the eight values of the frequency table.
The table lists FREQ CONT 0 to 7 with the frequencies 3.98, 5.56, 6.02, 6.37, 6.88, 9.63, 48.1 and 72.2 (Hz).
When LFO ON is 1, the LFO is on.
$24 is Timer-A, commented Timer-A upper 8 bits.
The $24 cell is drawn across the full width of the table.
$25 is Timer-A, commented Timer-A lower 2 bits.
The $25 cell is drawn with a filled left part and a Timer-A part at the right.
$26 is Timer-B, commented Timer-B Data.
The $26 cell is drawn across the full width of the table.
$31 to $3E are Detune/Multiple, with the cells DT and MULTI.
The cell is drawn as a filled left part, then DT, then MULTI.
$41 to $4E are Total Level, with the cell TL.
The cell is drawn as a filled left part, then TL.
$51 to $5E are Key Scale/Attack Rate, with the cells KS and AR.
The cell is drawn as KS, a filled part, then AR.
$61 to $6E are AMON/Decay Rate, with the cells AM and DR.
The cell is drawn as AM, a filled part, then DR.
In its description of $61 to $6E, D7 is AMON and D4 to D0 are DR; D6 and D5 are drawn filled.
DR is the Decay Rate.
AMON controls amplitude modulation for each slot, and is on when 1.
$11 is Control 2.
The $11 cell is drawn across the full width of the table.
In its description, $11 has L at D7 and R at D6; the other bits are drawn as -.
L: when 1, output goes to the left channel.
R: when 1, output goes to the right channel.
$12 is Start ADDR.(L).
$13 is Start ADDR.(H).
The $12 and $13 cells are drawn across the full width of the table.
In the description, the ROM address bits 23 to 0 are drawn as Start Address(H), Start Address(L) and a Fix Level of 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0.
The cells of $16 and $17 carry no label: each is drawn as a row of = signs.
The $16 and $17 cells are drawn across the full width of the table.
MAME stores writes to $16 and $17; its prescale value takes $16 as the low byte and bits 2 to 0 of $17 as the upper bits.
The cell of $18 carries no label: it is drawn as a row of = signs.
The $18 cell is drawn across the full width of the table.
MAME stores a write to $18 as the ADPCM-B CPU data byte.
While MAME's execute flag (bit 7 of ADPCM-B register 0) is set and record and external are clear, a $18 write clears its ready flag, per its comment.
$1B is EG Control.
The $1B cell is drawn across the full width of the table.
In its description, $1B is EG-Control across D7 to D0.
$1B is the ADPCM-B Output Level Control; all 1 is the maximum.
$1C is Flag Control.
The $1C cell is drawn across the full width of the table.
In its description, $1C has MSK B at D7, D6 with no MSK label and MSK A5 to MSK A0 at D5 to D0.
When a MSK bit is 1, the corresponding flag in Status 1 is 0.
A 1 in D7 or D5-D0 of $1C also clears the matching bit of MAME's latched end-of-sample status; a 1 in D7 clears the ADPCM-B end-of-sample status too.
$0D is the Envelop Shape Cycle (spelled so in the capture), with the labelled cells CON, ATT, ALT and HLD.
The $0D cell is drawn with a filled left part before its four labelled cells.
MAME sets its envelope state to 0 on a write of $0D, unless an SSG override is installed, which takes the write first.
$28 is Key-ON/OFF, with a Slot cell, a filled cell and a CH cell.
The $28 cell is drawn as a Slot part, a narrow filled part and a CH part.
$27 is Timer-A/B Control and 2 CH Mode, with the cells Mode, Reset B A, Enable B A and Load B A.
The $27 cell is drawn as four parts: Mode, Reset, Enable and Load, the last three each split into B and A.
MAME does not store a write of 0x27 at once: it hands the byte to a scheduler synchronisation, and the store happens when the engine's mode-write handler runs.
$10 is Control 1.
The $10 cell is drawn across the full width of the table.
In its description, $10 has START at D7, REPEAT at D4 and RESET at D0.
The description of $10 is headed ADPCM-B Start, Control external memory access.
RESET: a line in Japanese says that 1 during execution returns ADPCM-B to its initial state, and adds that REPEAT is 0.
REPEAT: when 1, ADPCM-B output repeats from the same addresses.
START: when 1, ADPCM-B output begins.
The other bits of $10 (D6, D5, D3, D2 and D1) are drawn as -.
MAME forces D5 of a written $10 to 1 and D6 to 0; its comment says external mode is forced on and recording disabled.
On RESET MAME stops playback and holds the output without clearing the externally visible playing flag, as its comment says.
$19 is Delta-N(L).
$1A is Delta-N(H).
The $19 and $1A cells are drawn across the full width of the table.
In the description, DELTA-N (H) and DELTA-N (L) are drawn as the 16-bit DELTA-N, d15 to d8 and d7 to d0.
The sampling rate is given as f = delta-N / 256 * 55.5 kHz; a translator's note says the original divided by 216.
MAME adds delta-N to a 16-bit position per call of its ADPCM-B clock and consumes a buffered nibble when the sum reaches 0x10000: a divisor of 65536, not 256.
$14 is End ADDR.(L).
$15 is End ADDR.(H).
The $14 and $15 cells are drawn across the full width of the table.
In the description, the ROM address bits 23 to 0 are drawn as End Address(H), End Address(L) and a Fix Level box.
The End Address drawing has a third box, Fix Level, holding 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0, after the End Address(H) and (L) boxes.
When the low 8 bits of MAME's address are all 1, it reports the end as hit if the address shifted right by 8 equals the end address.
MAME returns 0xFF for a read of register 0x0E or 0x0F; its comment says the I/O ports are not supported.
MAME handles a write of register 0x0E or 0x0F in a branch with no statement; its comment says the I/O ports are not supported.
MAME's SSG register array holds 0x10 bytes, and its accessors name 0x0E and 0x0F the I/O port A and B data.

searched.gave: ymfm_opn.h and ymopn.h cite no manual; ymfm_opn.cpp comments both branches of registers 0x0E and 0x0F as I/O ports not supported.
The YM2610 manual in the table draws its SSG table down to $0D; its allocation map (line 607) gives the SSG block as $00 to $0F, naming no I/O registers.

archive.org was not searched for a second YM2610 document; the manual in the table already lists its archive copy at web.archive.org.

rows.text: $71 to $7E are Sustain Rate, with the cell SR.
The cell is drawn as a filled part, then SR.
$81 to $8E are Sustain Level/Release Rate, with the cells SL and RR.
The cell is drawn as SL, then RR.
$91 to $9E are SSG-EG, described as the SSG-Type Envelop Control.
The cell is drawn as a filled part, then SSG-EG.
$A1 and $A2 are F-Num 1, listed under F-Numbers/Block.
The $A1,$A2 cell is one undivided cell holding F-Num 1.
MAME copies the low six bits latched by a write to 0xA4..0xA6 into the matching 0xA4..0xA6 register when 0xA0..0xA2 is written.
MAME returns from the register write without storing when the low two bits of the register number are 3, as for 0xA3.
$A5 and $A6 are Block and F-Num 2; the left part of the cell is drawn filled.
The cell is drawn as a filled part, then Block, then F-Num 2.
MAME latches only the low six bits of a write to 0xA4..0xA6 in an internal register, and copies them to the register only when 0xA0..0xA2 is next written.
$A9 and $AA are 2CH*F-Num 1, with the comment 2 CH - 2 Slot.
The $A9,$AA cell is one undivided cell holding 2 CH * F-Num 1.
MAME also reads 0xA8 as the frequency of the operator at offset 6 of channel 2, when the two top bits of 0x27 are not zero.
$AD and $AE are 2CH*Block and 2CH*F-Num2, with the comment F-Numbers/Block.
The cell is drawn as a filled part, then 2CH*Block, then 2CH*F-Num2.
MAME latches the low six bits of a write to 0xA4..0xA6 or 0xAC..0xAE, and applies them only when 0xA0..0xA2 or 0xA8..0xAA is next written.
$B1 and $B2 are FB and Connect, with the comment Self Feedback/Connection.
The cell is drawn as a filled part, then FB, then Connect.
$B5 and $B6 are L, R, AMS and PMS, with the comment LR SEL./AM,PM SENS.
The cell is drawn as L, R, AMS, a filled part, then PMS.
In its description of $B5-$B6, D7 is L, D6 is R, D5 and D4 are AMS and D2 to D0 are PMS.
In that description, D3 of $B5-$B6 is drawn filled.
PMS controls phase modulation and AMS controls amplitude modulation, each according to the table below it.
L and R specify the Left and Right channel output.
The PMS table gives the difference in cents for PMS 0 to 7: 0, then plus or minus 3.4, 6.7, 10, 14, 20, 40 and 80.
AMS 0 to 3 give a difference of 0, 1.44, 5.9 and 11.8 dB.
MAME's OPNA register reset stores 0xC0 in 0xB4..0xB6 and in 0x1B4..0x1B6, which the YM2610 uses.
MAME shifts the doubled LFO AM value right by 7, 3, 1 or 0 for AMS 0..3; its comment asks why full sensitivity gives 4.9 dB, not 11.8.
MAME stores a write to 0xB4..0xB6 and reads bits 5-4 as AMS and bits 2-0 as PMS; it names bits 7 and 6 output 0 and output 1.
MAME reads AMS at bits 5-4 and PMS at bits 2-0 of 0xB4..0xB6; bit 7 is its output 0 flag and bit 6 its output 1 flag.
MAME adds a channel's sample to its output 0 when bit 7 of 0xB4..0xB6 is set, and to its output 1 when bit 6 is set.
MAME's comment calls address 0xFF the ID code.
A data-port read with the address register at 0xFF returns the value 1.
A data-port write at address 0xFF goes to the FM register array, which stores the byte under that number.

searched.gave: ymfm_opn.h, ymopn.h and ymopn.cpp cite no manual; line 1928 of ymfm_opn.cpp comments the 0xFF read as 'FF: ID code'.
The manual in the table lists registers up to $B6 and names no ID code; its only $FF is the $1B data at line 1164.

rows.text: $00 is Dump/ADPCM-A ON, with the cells DM, a filled bit and AON.
The $00 cell is drawn as DM, a filled bit, then AON.
In its description, $00 has DM at D7 and AON across D5 to D0.
In that description, D6 of $00 is drawn as --.
DM set to 1 dumps the sound; DM at 0 produces a sound.
AON specifies the ADPCM-A channel control bits.
On a key on MAME loads the channel's read address from the start address registers and clears its nibble, byte, accumulator and step index.
$01 is ADPCM-A Total Level, with the cell ATL.
The $01 cell is drawn as a filled part, then ATL.
In its description, $01 has ATL across D5 to D0.
In that description, D7 and D6 of $01 are drawn as --.
ATL sets the ADPCM-A volume between 0 and -47.25 dB in steps of 0.75 dB.
ATL with all bits at 1 equals 0 dB.
MAME sums the channel and total attenuations, then uses multiplier 15 minus the sum's low three bits and shift 5 plus its high bits; a comment says to verify.
$02 is Test, with the comment LSI Test Data.
The $02 cell is one undivided cell holding Test.
The $02 address is provided to test the LSI.
The $02 value is usually all 0.
$08 to $0D are Output Select and Channel Level, with the cells L, R, a filled part and AC L.
The cell is drawn as L, R, a filled part, then AC L.
In its description of $08-0D, L is D7, R is D6 and ACL spans D5 to D0.
L: when 1, output goes to the Left channel.
R: when 1, output goes to the Right channel.
ACL sets each channel's level from 0 to -23.25 dB in steps of 0.75 dB.
ACL with all bits at 1 equals 0 dB.
MAME reads L and R from D7 and D6 but the channel level from the low five bits, mask 0x1F, so D5 takes no part.
MAME sums the channel and total attenuations, then uses multiplier 15 minus the sum's low three bits and shift 5 plus its high bits; a comment says to verify.
$10 to $15 are Start ADDR.(L), with the comment Start Address.
The $10 to $15 cell is one undivided cell holding Start ADDR.(L).
The description heads the start address registers as L/H, at $10 to $15 and $18 to $1D.
The drawing maps Start Address(H) to ROM address bits 23 to 16, Start Address(L) to bits 15 to 8 and a fixed level of 0 to bits 7 to 0.
$18 to $1D are Start ADDR.(H).
The $18 to $1D cell is one undivided cell holding Start ADDR.(H).
The D4 to D7 values of $18 to $1D and of $28 to $2D must be the same.
$20 to $25 are End ADDR.(L), with the comment End Address.
The $20 to $25 cell is one undivided cell holding End ADDR.(L).
The description heads the end address registers as L/H, at $20 to $25 and $28 to $2D.
The drawing maps End Address(H) to ROM address bits 23 to 16, End Address(L) to bits 15 to 8 and a fixed level of 0 to bits 7 to 0.
MAME adds 1 to the end value (H and L), shifts it left by 8 and stops when the 20 low bits match; its comment says the end is inclusive.
In the register map, $28 to $2D are labelled End ADDR.(L).
The $28 to $2D cell is one undivided cell holding End ADDR.(L), as the map labels it.
MAME takes 0x28 to 0x2D as the high byte of the end address, which it shifts left by 8 into the value it compares.
With A1 at 1, the register allocation map draws $30 to $B6 as FM, for CH3 and CH4.
With A1 at 0, the same map draws $30 to $B6 as FM, for CH1 and CH2.
MAME takes a write to the upper address port as 0x100 ORed with the data, and its upper data port sends addresses from 0x130 to the FM engine.
MAME's YM2610 defaults its FM channel mask to 0x36, bits 1, 2, 4 and 5, and passes it to the FM clock and output calls.
MAME reads an operator's detune and multiple from register 0x30 plus its operator offset.
MAME reads total level of an operator at register 0x40 plus its operator offset, which adds 0x100 for each group of 12 operators.
MAME stores the byte written to 0x140..0x14F in the FM register array under that number.

searched.gave: ymfm_opn.h and ymopn.h cite no manual; the comments in ymfm_opn.h only list the register bit layout.
The YM2610 manual in the table draws its allocation map (lines 604 to 617, held by ym2610:register:0x130..0x13F) and the total level 2 cell once, with no bank.
